items: exponent alignment — Express operands using the same power of two.
rounding — Choose a nearby representable value for an exact result.
truncation — Discard bits beyond the available precision.
overflow — Numerical result exceeds the representable range.
precision loss — Significant binary information cannot be stored.

questions.prompt: Choose the response that best addresses this independent task: Foundation · 1 OF 3 Why must exponents be aligned before binary floating-point addition?
questions.answer: So corresponding mantissa bits represent the same place values.
options: So corresponding mantissa bits represent the same place values.
Align B to 0.0100 × 2³. Subtract: 0.1010 − 0.0100 = 0.0110 × 2³. Shift left and decrease exponent: 0.1100 × 2² = 3. No shown bits are discarded.
Right-shifting may discard significant low-order bits. They cannot all be held in the available mantissa, so rounding or truncation can produce an inexact result.
questions.feedback: So corresponding mantissa bits represent the same place values.
